::: {#rem-universal-tm}
#### Interpreters are universal machines

A Python interpreter is a universal machine in the sense of @thm-universal-tm:
one fixed program that runs any other program it is given as input.
@arora2009computational [section 1.4] state @thm-universal-tm
with the bound $C \, T \log_2 T$.
The $\strlen{w}$ term added here counts the steps $U$ spends reading past $w$,
which can be long because of padding,
and $T + 1$ keeps the bound positive when $T = 1$.
They prove a version with $C \, T^2$ in place of $C \, T \log_2 T$
by an argument like that of @rem-tm-robustness-proof,
and they prove the stronger bound in section 1.7.
The [Kolmogorov complexity](kolmogorov-complexity.qmd#def-kolmogorov-complexity)
of a string is defined with a universal machine that,
unlike the one of @thm-universal-tm,
reads a single program,
and [halts](#def-turing-machine) only on programs none of which is a prefix of another.

:::
